newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries in London down slightly before data.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries in London down slightly before data.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices in London were slightly down on Friday in what traders called a fairly quiet session ahead of pre-weekend economic data.
"Current levels don't appear to be particularly attractive to new buyers entering the market," said Technical Data fixed income analyst Andy Cossor, in London.
The U.S. long bond at 1127 GMT was at 100-26 yielding 6.440 percent, against 100-30 at the Tokyo close and 101-01 at Thursday's close in New York.
December T-bond futures were at 115-04, 5/32 down on the Thursday Chicago settlement.

Capacity utilisation for October is expected to come in at 83.0 percent compared with 83.3 percent previously. Industrial production for October is forecast by the market at a 0.2 percent increase, the same as for September. Both sets of data are due at 1415 GMT.
Dick Howard, senior economist at Julius Baer Investments, said the data were unlikely to have any dramatic impact, but risk was more to the downside.
"If industrial production comes in flat, then the market will probably not do anything but if it comes in at plus 0.3 or plus 0.5 percent then you could see some downside action," He said.

Howard said market sentiment was that the long bond could try for a 6.38 percent yield target in the medium term. But most players in the market were now fairly long and it would need "something fairly special" to get it through that level.
Cossor said the market looked overbought and was bound to be affected by profit-taking at some stage although the market had kept on "defying gravity" by making new highs on Thursday.
He said that interest in Treasuries in the London session was greatest in the two-and 10-year sectors.

The two-year T-note was trading at 100-12 to yield 5.667 percent, just under the Tokyo and New York closes at 100-13. The 10-year T-note was at 102-15, to yield 6.162 percent compared with 102-16 in Tokyo and 102-18 in New York. -- Stephen Nisbet, International Bonds Unit +44 171 6320
